authority_relationship: This statement certificate supplies the exact expression, environment, source-selection rationale, mutations, and validation details referenced by the reconciled per-theorem instance manifest; it is not a parallel lifecycle authority.
canonical_name: Erdos-Ko-Rado maximum size of a uniform intersecting family
canonical_statement: For all natural numbers n and r with 1 <= r <= n / 2, the maximum cardinality of an intersecting family of r-element subsets of the labeled ground set Fin n is choose(n - 1, r - 1): a star attains this cardinality and every such family has at most this cardinality.

source_selection.repository_claim: Docs/researches/math_theorems.md:6040-6045 and duplicate :7036-7041: maximum size of an intersecting family
source_selection.citation: P. Erdos, Chao Ko, and R. Rado, Intersection theorems for systems of finite sets, Quarterly Journal of Mathematics (2) 12 (1961), 313-320, DOI 10.1093/qmath/12.1.313
source_selection.sharpness_locator: printed page 314, the following best-possible construction
source_selection.variant_decision: The complete catalog gloss asks for a maximum size, so the root is the standard uniform-family maximum-value formulation: it includes the universal upper bound and an attaining star. The original at-most-size antichain theorem is broader in its premises, while an upper bound alone does not establish a maximum. A classification of all equality families is stronger than the gloss and is excluded, particularly at the included n = 2r boundary where no uniqueness claim is made.
source_selection.review_boundary: The primary theorem and sharpness remark support this provisional selection, but complete accountable translation, correction or errata review, proof mapping, independent H0 review, and master acceptance remain open.

domain_and_universes: n r : Nat; A : Finset (Finset (Fin n)); the target and all predicates are propositions in Lean universe 0.
quantifiers: every n r : Nat with 1 <= r <= n / 2
some attaining family A : Finset (Finset (Fin n))
every bounded family A : Finset (Finset (Fin n))
hypotheses: the uniform rank r is positive
the universally bounded family is intersecting
every member of the universally bounded family has cardinality r
conclusion: There exists an intersecting r-uniform family with card choose(n - 1, r - 1), and every intersecting r-uniform family has card at most choose(n - 1, r - 1).

encoding_decisions.ground_set: Fin n is the labeled n-element ground set named literally in the canonical human claim and used by the pinned formal candidate. No unproved transport from an arbitrary finite type is credited.
encoding_decisions.family: Finset (Finset (Fin n)) represents a finite duplicate-free family of finite subsets.
encoding_decisions.uniformity: Set.Sized r on the coerced family fixes every member cardinality to r; fixed-size distinct members are automatically incomparable.
encoding_decisions.intersecting: Set.Intersecting requires all member pairs, including self-pairs, to be non-disjoint. The checked sized_intersecting_iff_pairwise bridge proves equivalence to distinct-pair intersection when 1 <= r.
encoding_decisions.maximum: Attainability and the universal bound are conjoined. The checked alternate chooses the concrete star of all r-subsets containing one point.
encoding_decisions.range: The source-positive premise 1 <= r is retained, while r <= n / 2 includes the equality boundary. This range implies n is nonzero, so a star center exists.
encoding_decisions.bound: Natural subtraction and Nat.choose use mathlib conventions exactly as (n - 1).choose (r - 1).
encoding_decisions.boundary: No admissible positive rank exists for n = 0 or n = 1. The n = 4, r = 2 equality boundary is kernel-checked to have an attaining star.
encoding_decisions.equality_classification: The target fixes only the maximum value. It neither asserts stars are the only extremizers nor excludes non-star equality families at n = 2r.

minimal_import_result: A canonical-target-only fixture elaborates with exactly the two direct imports. Deleting either declared import causes the fixture to fail: Intersecting supplies Set.Intersecting, while Slice supplies Set.Sized and Nat.choose. The full statement and concrete-star transport module also elaborates.
minimal_import_boundary: This proves necessity among the declared imports for the canonical target fixture, not global minimality across every differently factored collection or transitive dependency closure. The proof-bearing Mathlib.Combinatorics.SetFamily.KruskalKatona module is deliberately absent.

alternate_encodings.boundary: The alternate replaces the existential attaining family with an explicit star and retains the identical universal upper-bound component.

alternate_encodings.target: distinct-pair intersection on positive uniform families
alternate_encodings.boundary: This local semantic bridge is parameterized by the positive-rank and uniformity hypotheses; it does not identify the r = 0 singleton-empty-family convention.

excluded_degenerate_cases: r = 0 is excluded by 1 <= r because self-pair intersection and the source distinct-pair convention diverge on the singleton empty-set family
n = 0 and n = 1 have no admissible positive r under r <= n / 2
included_boundary_cases: empty and singleton families whenever they satisfy the stated hypotheses
the equality boundary r = n / 2, including n = 4 and r = 2
natural-number subtraction in n - 1 and r - 1 under the positive admissible range
